1.why: Every MFA endpoint calls authorized(), which derives the account solely from session.userId set server-side; no client-supplied user identifier is ever accepted, so IDOR is not possible.

2.why: Codes are stored per-session and randomly generated in production, but DEMO_MODE (default outside production) uses the fixed code '123456' that would work for anyone running the demo.

3.why: Session rotation happens only at sign-in; enabling MFA (authenticator/verify, backup/confirm) never invalidates other existing sessions, so prior sessions remain valid afterward.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted (account.secret = encrypt(secret)) and backup codes are retained only as peppered SHA-256 hashes in the backups map.

5.why: Production uses crypto-strong randomBytes/randomInt for secrets, identity codes, and backup codes, but DEMO_MODE substitutes hardcoded deterministic codes.

6.why: The only cookie (mfa_session) is HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict, and secrets/CSRF/codes live only in JS memory variables with no localStorage or non-HttpOnly cookie use.

7.why: Server-side validators (emailOK, otpOK, codeOK), a method allow-list, and a 10KB body cap are enforced; data is in-memory so no SQL injection surface exists.

8.why: All dynamic values are inserted via textContent/createElement in a static template with a nonce-based CSP, so no user-controlled markup or script can execute.

9.why: The server issues no redirects at all (only JSON/404 responses) and the client uses only fixed hash anchors, so there is no open-redirect surface.

10.why: securityHeaders sets a nonce-based CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY on every response.

11.why: cookieValue() sets the session cookie with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict plus a Max-Age, and the clear cookie mirrors those attributes.

12.why: Server logging is clean and errors are generic, but DEMO_MODE intentionally console.logs identity codes, authenticator codes, and recovery codes, and the otpauth:// provisioning URI embeds the seed in a query string.

13.why: Identity codes are single-use (used flag) with a 10-minute expiry and backup codes are consumed on use, but TOTP authenticator codes remain reusable within the ±1 period drift window.

14.why: Four independent failure counters (sign-in, identity, authenticator, recovery) lock for 15 minutes after 5 failures, and code requests are additionally throttled to 3 per 15 minutes.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the old session and issues a fresh ID, getSession enforces 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
